experiment: Polymarket BTC 5-minute binaries: taker v1 vs passive makers
headline: Collecting: 40 of 200 settled windows before any arm is scored. Numbers below are running totals, not results.

arms.name: taker_v1
arms.description: The original tool, unchanged: buys the ask when N(d2) beats ask + taker fee, polling REST every 3s.

arms.name: maker_mid
arms.description: Rests quotes around the Polymarket mid. No outside information -- measures what passive quoting alone is worth.

arms.name: maker_model
arms.description: Rests quotes around the N(d2) model price.

arms.name: maker_anchored
arms.description: Rests quotes around the Polymarket mid moved by the spot-implied change since its recent average.

kill_criteria: A maker arm whose mean PnL per window is below zero at 95% confidence after 200 settled windows is stopped.
A maker arm with a negative mean 5s markout after 500 fills is being picked off; stopped.
These were written before the first paper fill (2026-09-25) and are not moved after seeing results.
caveats: Every maker reads BTC as a spread-weighted Binance + OKX mid; the taker keeps its original Binance feed. Maker windows are counted from 2026-09-25, when they moved to the composite.
Paper fills. A resting order joins the back of its price level, goes live 0.4s after it is sent, and fills only when a real print reaches it; a cancel takes 0.4s and can still be filled meanwhile.
Maker rebates are ignored and the taker pays the published fee, so the maker side is understated.
Only prints on the websocket move the paper queue; hidden or cross-matched liquidity is not modelled.
One process, one laptop: windows lost to sleep or a network drop are lost for every arm at once.
